description: Issue summary: Between 14:30 and 16:10 UTC on multiple days the customer's dedicated pool experienced a sustained throughput plateau with elevated p99 latency despite steady request rate. Impact: BrightAd's real-time scoring pipeline saw 30-40% drop in completed requests and increased client timeouts. Environment: Dedicated capacity (reserved pool), us-east-1, production. Observed behavior reproducible during the customer's peak window but not in staging.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Target the customer's dedicated route /v1/generate with model redwood-7b-v1 using standard batch config. 2) Send steady stream of 20 q/s of short requests (avg tokens 25) for 30 minutes during a simulated 'afternoon' window. 3) Observe autoscaler not provisioning additional slots and p99 climbing while GPU utilization remains uneven across nodes. Note: issue reproduces only when a background tenant prefetch pattern is present (see hypothesis).
logs:
- Grafana panel: /d/redwood/dedicated-pool-io?orgId=1&var-cluster=reserved-us-east shows p99 jump at 14:34 UTC
- Scheduler logs: scheduler-2026-03-10.log lines 1432-1450: "slot_assign: delay_reason=kv-prefetch_backpressure"
- Serving runtime trace: trace_id=bd3a1f: repeated RPC queue stalls on node gpu-az2-17
- Customer application logs: client-side timeouts 504 at ~14:35 UTC
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: hidden background prefetcher from another tenant was creating short, high-frequency streams that fragmented batch slots and heated local KV-cache growth, causing the autoscaler to misclassify capacity headroom. Evidence: 1) Correlated small-stream spike from tenant t-9765 in sidecar logs. 2) KV cache hit-rate dropped on affected nodes and memory pressure rose, triggering internal preemptive eviction. 3) Autoscaler telemetry showed suppressed scaling due to noisy heartbeats from overloaded nodes rather than global bin counts. Additional findings: NIC-level I/O latency on NVLink was elevated on two nodes coincident with the plateau. We opened INT-4523 to track node-level hardware noise. Temporary mitigation toggled per-route conservative batching which reduced p99 but increased per-token cost.
comments: Support (Maya Chen) - 2026-03-10: Customer reports repeated afternoon dips in throughput starting last Thursday. Provided initial trace bundle and Grafana links. Marked as P1 given production impact.

SRE (Ravi Patel) - 2026-03-10: Observed short-stream fanout from tenant t-9765 between 14:30-15:10 UTC. Sidecar metrics show bursty prefetch RPCs. Scheduling logs indicate repeated slot churn on gpu-az2-17 and gpu-az2-19.
Customer (BrightAd Ops - Elena Ortiz) - 2026-03-10: We saw client-side 504s around 14:35 and fallback to batch queue. This window is our busiest ad-serving period.

SRE (Ravi Patel) - 2026-03-11: Deployed conservative per-route batching and disabled cross-tenant prefetch for t-9765 in the reserved pool as a temporary measure. Immediate p99 improvement observed from 420ms -> 220ms.

Eng (Kai Morales) - 2026-03-11: Root cause looks like combined effect of KV cache growth plus a quiet-period in the autoscaler's decision loop that ignored transient I/O stalls. Preparing PR to add short-window fairness signals to autoscaler (see PR #1189).

Support (Maya Chen) - 2026-03-12: Customer confirmed throughput normalized across the usual peak window after temporary mitigation. Agreed to schedule follow-up for permanent backend fix and review of tenant prefetch policies.
resolution: Workaround applied: disabled cross-tenant background prefetch on the reserved cluster for tenant t-9765 and enabled conservative per-route batching for BrightAd's route. Result: p99 latency reduced ~48% and throughput returned to baseline during peak. Engineering fix: merged PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1189 to surface short-window fairness signal into autoscaler and to add KV-cache throttling heuristics when per-node eviction > 15%. Rollout: staged to us-east reserved pool on 2026-03-12 during low-traffic maintenance window. Follow-ups: (1) SRE to monitor node-level NVLink I/O and file INT-4523 for hardware noise long-term, (2) Product to review tenant prefetch config defaults for dedicated pools. Ticket resolved after customer validation on 2026-03-12.
